scope: Cross-surface attack chains: kiosk+mobile sandwich, web→POS→mobile drift exploits, identity-theft via leaked credentials

attack_scenarios.name: Kiosk-mobile sandwich double-redeem
attack_scenarios.scenario: Attacker has stolen victim's phone number (leaked from receipt, social engineering, public Facebook). Attacker (1) opens own mobile-app, signs in to victim's account somehow (separate attack — but credentials often weak) OR (2) attacker uses victim's loyalty_code at kiosk while victim simultaneously opens own mobile-app and clicks 'Redeem'. Two concurrent /api/loyalty/redeem calls with same loyalty_code from two surfaces. PLOY-2-DBA-01 + PLOY-3-DBA-02 = both succeed if balance covers both. Victim loses points to orphan row.

attack_scenarios.name: Cashier shoulder-surfs customer phone, harvests loyalty_code, redeems on next shift
attack_scenarios.scenario: Cashier types customer's phone into /api/loyalty/check (auth:sanctum allows any logged-in user — kiosk machine OR staff session). Server returns name + balance + loyalty_code. Cashier writes code on note. Next day, cashier alone at POS calls /api/loyalty/redeem with staff session → isStaff branch (line 259) bypasses ownership → points deducted. Customer doesn't notice until next mobile-app refresh.
attack_scenarios.remediation: Multi-layer: (a) /loyalty/check returns loyalty_code ONLY if caller is the customer themselves (caller.id === user.id), OR mask the code (return last 4 chars); (b) audit-log every /loyalty/check + /loyalty/redeem with caller_id; (c) disable isStaff branch on redeem (PLOY-2-S-01).

attack_scenarios.name: Mobile-app QR replay across kiosks within scan-window
attack_scenarios.scenario: QR encodes loyalty_code (or FK:loyalty_code per LoyaltyController::scan line 611). Code is static. Attacker watches victim at kiosk A, photographs QR, walks to kiosk B in same chain, scans photographed QR → kiosk B server resolves victim's User → attacker can redeem at kiosk B with victim's points.
attack_scenarios.outcome: VULNERABLE if QR is static. PLOY-2-R-04 same family.
attack_scenarios.verdict: FAIL for static QR. Mobile spec loyalty-03-qr-refresh implies QR rotates — need to verify the mobile implementation.
attack_scenarios.remediation: TOTP-style rotating QR (60s validity) or signed-and-time-limited QR payload. Server validates QR signature + timestamp at /api/frontend/loyalty/scan.

attack_scenarios.name: Web-account-page-discloses-loyalty-code-via-XSS
attack_scenarios.scenario: If web surface adds an account page showing loyalty_code (per PLOY-3-A-03 deferred feature), and the page is vulnerable to XSS, attacker steals loyalty_code via DOM injection.
attack_scenarios.outcome: FORWARD-LOOKING. Web has no loyalty integration yet — moot for V1.
attack_scenarios.verdict: DEFERRED. Address at V1.0.2 web-account-page feature.
attack_scenarios.remediation: When web adds loyalty UI: CSP + sanitize all customer-input fields + show loyalty_code only after explicit user click (defense-in-depth).

attack_scenarios.name: Cross-surface manual_add fraud via admin-as-staff
attack_scenarios.scenario: Compromised admin account (or rogue branch manager) calls POST /api/loyalty/add-points with arbitrary code + points. LoyaltyController::addPoints line 188-191 allows ['Admin', 'Branch Manager', 'POS Operator', 'Stuff']. Admin credits 100k pts to own account → redeems = €1000 free.
attack_scenarios.outcome: VULNERABLE. Mitigated by manager-review audit but not by code.
attack_scenarios.remediation: (a) Restrict /add-points to ['Admin', 'Branch Manager'] only (not POS Operator/Stuff), (b) cap points per manual_add (e.g. max 500/day per staff), (c) audit-log every manual_add to chain-signed audit_logs (cross-ref PLOY-3-S-03), (d) require dual-approval for points > threshold.

attack_scenarios.name: Source-surface forgery for analytics evasion
attack_scenarios.scenario: If source_surface becomes user-controllable param (e.g. via PLOY-3-A-01 remediation that accepts 'source' from request), an attacker on mobile can label their redemption as 'kiosk' to confuse downstream analytics.
attack_scenarios.outcome: FORWARD-LOOKING — depends on remediation choice. If 'source' is request-controlled, must be cross-checked against actual auth context (caller's token ability).
attack_scenarios.remediation: Server derives source_surface from auth context (not user input). Combine token.ability + role + User-Agent.

attack_scenarios.name: Refund-spoofing via order-cancel-without-original-redeem
attack_scenarios.scenario: Cancellation handler calls LoyaltyService::refundPoints which sums all redeem txns for the order_id. What if an attacker INSERTs a redeem txn for an order_id they don't own (e.g. via SQL injection — unlikely in Eloquent) then triggers cancel of that order?
attack_scenarios.outcome: PREVENTED at application layer. No SQL injection vector found. LoyaltyTransaction Eloquent inserts are parameterized.

attack_scenarios.name: GDPR-purge race during active redemption
attack_scenarios.scenario: Customer opts out → users record deleted → CASCADE deletes loyalty_transactions (FK ON DELETE CASCADE per migration line 32). If a redeem transaction is mid-flight (lockForUpdate held), the DELETE waits. After lock released, DELETE cascade purges. Pending redeem ledger (order_id=NULL) — orphaned.
attack_scenarios.verdict: ADVISORY. Anonymize-on-opt-out (PLOY-3-S-05) is the cleaner pattern.

primary_concerns: PLOY-3-R-01 kiosk-mobile sandwich race — chained dedup_key fix
PLOY-3-R-02 cashier shoulder-surf chain — needs /check restriction + audit-log
PLOY-3-R-05 admin manual_add abuse — needs cap + dual-approval

blocker_for_v1: For LeCayenne single-resto under owner-supervision: PASS-WITH-RISK. For chain rollout: BLOCKER. Recommend V1.0.2 hardening cycle on loyalty before chain-restaurant deployment.
